name: Provider Data Mis-match — ANZ.1 ancillary provider location missing
description: Identify PX_ANZ and check the event hierarchy, confirm the claim is Ancillary DME from the POS and procedure code, find the Ancillary Provider details blank, read the patient address off the claim image, enter the Type, ZIP and State, Validate and Pay.

steps.name: Identify the ANZ event and check the event hierarchy
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. The application displays every edit the claim hit, and PX_ANZ is the current event requiring review — an ancillary-provider event raised by missing patient-location details in Additional Claim Data. Read down the All Edits list in hierarchy order and check the Severity beside each code to determine whether any event must be resolved before PX_ANZ. If one is, resolve it first in hierarchy order; if none is, carry on. Here every event is Informational, so you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Event Resolution tab is clicked while this step is active. It is the tab the workspace opens on, so the click is a deliberate one.
steps.hint: On 'Event Resolution', the All Edits list shows PX_ANZ marked (Active), and a Severity beside every code. Read them all before moving on.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the ANZ event and check the event hierarchy

steps.name: Confirm the claim is an Ancillary DME service
steps.description: Before correcting anything, establish what kind of claim this is. Open the Claim Lines tab and read two fields on line one together: the Place of Service in the POS field, and the Procedure code. A claim billed with POS 12 and procedure code E0601 is an Ancillary DME claim. That matters for what comes later — the Ancillary Provider Type on an ancillary DME claim is the patient-location indicator, P. Here the POS is 12 and the procedure is E0601, so you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Lines tab is clicked while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Lines', read line one's POS and Procedure columns together — one without the other does not establish an ancillary DME claim.
steps.checklistItem: Confirm the claim is an Ancillary DME service

steps.name: Check the blank Ancillary Provider details
steps.description: Go to the Claim Data tab and open the Details sub-tab, then scroll to the Additional Claim Data section and read the values in the Ancillary Provider sub-section. All three — Type, ZIP and State — are blank. That is why the ANZ event fired: the claim carries no patient-location details at all. Nothing on these adjudication screens can fill them, so the next step is to find them somewhere else.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Details sub-tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Data' → 'Details', scroll to Additional Claim Data and find the Ancillary Provider sub-section. Read all three boxes before moving on — they are empty.
steps.checklistItem: Check the blank Ancillary Provider details

steps.name: Identify the patient address on the claim image
steps.description: Open the Claim Image tab. This is the scanned claim form the provider actually submitted — the document of record, against which the keyed-in claim system is only an approximation. Under Claim Image – Member Details, in the Patient section, find the Address field and read the patient's address, state and ZIP code from it. Those are the patient-location details the Ancillary Provider sub-section is missing, and this is the only place on the claim that carries them.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Image tab is clicked while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Image', open Member Details and read the Address field in the Patient section. The state and the ZIP are both inside that one line — note them before you go back.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the patient address on the claim image

steps.name: Open the Ancillary Provider section for update
steps.description: Now that you have the patient's location from the claim image, return to the Claim Data tab → Details sub-tab → Additional Claim Data section and open the Ancillary Provider sub-section again. In step 3 you were reading what was there; this time you are going to fill it in, using the details you just identified on the claim image.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Details sub-tab is opened again while this step is active. The trip to Claim Image closed the sub-tab strip, so this is a fresh, deliberate visit rather than the one step 3 already graded.
steps.hint: Back on 'Claim Data' → 'Details', scroll to Additional Claim Data → Ancillary Provider. The three boxes are editable.
steps.checklistItem: Open the Ancillary Provider section for update

steps.name: Enter the Type, ZIP and State values
steps.description: Fill all three Ancillary Provider boxes. Type is the patient-location indicator: on an ancillary DME claim billed with POS 12 — which you confirmed in step 2 — it takes P. The ZIP and the State both come from the patient's Address on the claim image you have just read: take the state abbreviation and the five-digit ZIP out of that line. Enter all three before you validate; the Validate button on the claim summary bar checks every one of them.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Graded on the State box, the last of the three in the document's own order. Completing this step is not enough to finish: the Validate guard in step 7 checks Type, ZIP and State together, so a trainee who fills only this box is refused there with nothing banked.
steps.hint: Type takes the patient-location indicator for an ancillary DME claim. ZIP and State are both inside the Address line you read on the claim image.
steps.checklistItem: Enter the Type, ZIP and State values

steps.name: Validate the updated details
steps.description: Check the three values you have entered against the patient address on the claim image, then click Validate on the claim summary bar at the top of the workspace, next to Submit. Validate is refused unless all three are correct, and the Validation line in the Ancillary Provider section says so. Once it passes, the ANZ event is resolved.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the guard holds — all three of Type, ZIP and State correct. The claim summary Validate is the only control that dispatches it. A refused press banks nothing, completes nothing, and writes the corrective message to the Validation line.
steps.hint: Validate sits on the claim summary bar, next to Submit. Re-read the Address on the claim image against what you typed before pressing it — a wrong value in any one of the three boxes refuses the whole press.

steps.name: Submit Pay decision
steps.description: The ANZ event is resolved and the claim carries the patient-location details it was missing. Nothing else on the claim is in dispute, so it is paid. Go to the Decision section in the header, select Pay from the dropdown and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when Pay is submitted. Any other decision leaves the step incomplete and scores zero for the decision.
steps.hint: Select 'Pay' in the header Decision dropdown, then Submit.
